title: Context Switching
body:
Saving enough machine state that execution can be resumed later as if nothing had
happened, then restoring it. In this course it is the hardware fact underneath every
interrupt: an [[IRQs|IRQ]] arrives mid-instruction-stream, the [[CPU]] jumps to an
[[ISRs|ISR]], and the interrupted program has to be unable to tell.

What has to be preserved on the [[Motorola 68000]]:

- The program counter and the [[Status Register]], pushed automatically by the hardware
  when the interrupt is taken
- Every data and address register the ISR touches, pushed by the ISR itself:

```MC68000 ASM
    movem.l    d0-d2/a0-a2,-(sp)
    ; ISR body
    movem.l    (sp)+,d0-d2/a0-a2
    rte
```

Note `rte` (return from exception) rather than `rts`: it pops the status register too.

Because the ISR runs on the interrupted program's stack and in the middle of whatever it
was doing, anything it shares with the main program is a [[Concurrency]] hazard.

[[OPERATING SYSTEMS]] takes this same mechanism and makes it the basis of multitasking: a
context switch between [[Processes]] is the interrupt save/restore plus swapping the
memory map, and the fact that it costs real time is what limits how short a scheduling
quantum can usefully be.
